title: Ants on a backlogged scheduler, with and without the fix
question: Which of these looks like a colony behaving normally?
context_md:
**This corrects the framing of my earlier card** ("An ant's intended walking pace"). That one said the creature code was doing everything on time -- true for an undisturbed world, and I had not yet measured a dug-out one.

Measured on the world the game actually ships (8192x2560), with the pick swung at play rate -- 299 cuts over the run, about two minutes of digging:

| frame | sites the scheduler served | of which structural | **of which creature** | still pending |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2,400 | 41 | 7 | **27** | 5,029 |
| 3,600 | **2,000 -- the cap** | 1,974 | **11** | 20,467 |
| 4,800 | **2,000 -- the cap** | 1,964 | **0** | 43,321 |
| 6,000 | **2,000 -- the cap** | 1,926 | **0** | 62,658 |

Creature ticks share one per-frame budget with structural checks. A structural check is scheduled *due now*, so a backlogged one is stuck in the past; an ant reschedules itself into the future; the queue is sorted by due-time. So once the backlog is deeper than the budget the ant is not merely behind in the queue -- it cannot be reached at all.

Only the creatures show it because sand, water and fire never go through this queue.

Left: the colony with that backlog in front of it. Right: the same world, same frames, with creature ticks given their own reserved budget.
